mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Evoque D200 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover Evoque D200 engine typically costs between £3,500 and £7,000 for the unit itself, depending on the level of rebuild. Used units can be found from £2,000, but carry higher risk for a complex MHEV diesel. Supply and fit labour will add approximately £650-£910 depending on the specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil dilution in a Range Rover Evoque D200?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your AJ20D4 engine. Look for rising oil level on the dipstick between services, or a strong diesel smell from the oil filler cap. The DPF warning light or reduced fuel economy may also indicate incomplete regeneration cycles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Evoque D200?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely, given the high retained values of the L551 MHEV Evoque range. A rebuilt AJ20D4 engine with upgraded timing chain components and revised piston rings can extend the vehicle's life significantly. For vehicles valued over £14,000, a warranted reconditioned engine protects your investment far better than a cheap used unit.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the D200 and D180/D240 Evoque engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The D200 uses the AJ20D4 2.0-litre Ingenium diesel tuned to 204hp with 48V mild-hybrid assistance. The D180 uses a lower-output tune (163hp) of the same architecture, also with MHEV. The D240 (discontinued) was a twin-turbo variant producing 240hp, with a higher failure rate due to increased cylinder pressures.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Evoque D200 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straightforward supply and fit of a reconditioned AJ20D4 engine typically takes 3 to 5 days at a specialist workshop. This allows time for 48V MHEV system reset, proper bedding-in procedures, ECU calibration, and a thorough road test.

mainEntity.name: Does the D200 MHEV system need special handling during engine replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the 48V mild-hybrid system requires specialist attention during engine replacement. The belt-integrated starter generator (BiSG) and 48V battery must be inspected and properly reintegrated. Not all garages are qualified for MHEV work - confirm hybrid training before booking.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Evoque D200 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Evoque D200 is celebrated for its refined mild-hybrid diesel efficiency and punchy 204hp output, but the AJ20D4 Ingenium engine requires vigilant maintenance to avoid its well-documented failure modes. The AJ20D4 2.0L MHEV Diesel dominates replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components, such as revised timing chain tensioners and improved piston ring designs, addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Dilution & DPF Regeneration Failure - Why the Range Rover Evoque D200 AJ20D4 Loses Lubrication
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 40,000-80,000 miles (directly linked to driving pattern, not age)
problems.rootCause: Frequent short journeys prevent the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles. Unburned diesel fuel passes into the sump during regeneration attempts, raising oil levels, thinning viscosity, and destroying the oil's ability to protect bearings, timing components, and turbos.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Oil Dilution Mitigation (Flush & Software Update)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full oil and filter change (two flushes), DPF static regeneration, PCM software update to modify regen strategy.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early (rising oil level but no knocking). Temporary fix if driving pattern doesn't change.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has suffered bottom-end knock or seized from heavily diluted oil.

problems.recommendation: If your Evoque D200 is exhibiting early signs of oil dilution (rising oil level, diesel smell from filler cap) or timing chain rattle on cold start, act immediately. A specialist oil flush and software update (£250-£500) or preventative chain replacement (£1,200-£1,800) can save the engine. However, if the engine has already suffered bottom-end knock or seized, a full reconditioned replacement is the most reliable long-term investment.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Range Rover Evoque D200 AJ20D4 Rattles on Startup
problems.affectedModels: Range Rover Evoque D200 (AJ20D4, 2020-present, particularly pre-November 2019 builds)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner relies on consistent oil pressure. Oil dilution from DPF issues accelerates tensioner wear, leading to chain slack, guide breakage, and eventual chain jump or seizure.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Preventative Timing Chain & Tensioner Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides, cam sprockets), oil pump chain, and perform full oil system flush.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught before chain jump. Adds 60k+ miles if upgraded parts used.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the chain has already jumped timing or the engine has suffered valve damage.
